fatal_errors: The proposed polycrystalline material class conflicts with the target's homogenized equiatomic FCC Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni-derived single crystals.
Grain-boundary sliding is inapplicable to the tested bulk single crystals and is not a mechanism supported by the target study.
The hypothesis omits the distinct cryogenic inertial dulling, MSAD-controlled solid-solution strengthening, and high-temperature Portevin-Le Chatelier regimes.
No specific alloy composition, crystallographic orientation, temperature range, strain rate, or quantitative outcome is identified.
explanation: The response recognizes only the generic fact that temperature affects plastic deformation and uses room temperature as a baseline. It does not reconstruct the relevant Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni-derived FCC single-crystal materials or the compression/CRSS measurements from 9–1373 K. Its emphasis on polycrystallinity and grain-boundary sliding is inconsistent with the experiment. It also misses the observed near-doubling of CRSS on cooling, phonon-drag-controlled inertial dulling below roughly 60–77 K, the correlation between extrapolated strength and MSAD, and Mn/Fe-dependent serrated PL strengthening at elevated temperature. The suggested TEM/XRD experiment and falsification rule are too nonspecific to discriminate among the target mechanisms.
